title: Project
text:
UNDER CONSTRUCTIONSpring 2027 preparation is in progress. Schedules, materials, and course policies are provisional.
The project follows the Spring 2026 MATH 563 requirements. The same project requirements apply to MATH 563 and MATH 574 in Spring 2027. Course-specific submission and scheduling links will be added when available.
You are required to complete a course project. The goal is to practice communicating statistical ideas clearly and critically—like you are reporting to colleagues whether a line of work is worth pursuing.

title: Project
text:
Types
Choose one of the following project types:

Research article review
Pick a scholarly research article related to topics in statistical inference (e.g., estimation, testing, likelihood/Bayes, asymptotics, bootstrap, identifiability, robustness, missing data, multiple testing, etc.) that does not duplicate a topic discussed in class. Your article must be different from your classmates’ choices.
Simulation or data analysis study
Design and carry out a focused study that uses computation to investigate a statistical question. Examples:

Analyze a data set of interest, but go beyond any existing analysis,
Compare procedures (power, bias, coverage, MSE) under realistic departures from assumptions,
Illustrate a theorem/asymptotic approximation with finite-sample behavior,
Replicate and critique an empirical claim from a paper,
Build a small method “pipeline” (e.g., model selection + inference) and evaluate it.

title: Project
text:
Submission

Submit your project topic using the Spring 2027 topic submission form when it is available. The deadline is listed in the course schedule; dates not yet listed remain TBD. Revised topics use the same course form.
After the topic deadline, check the course topic list to confirm approval and double-check presentation arrangements. The Spring 2027 form and topic-list links will be added after setup.
Prepare a 15-minute oral presentation (+5 minutes for questions) and a handout for the audience.

title: Project
text:
Presentations and observations

Consult the course schedule for presentation dates and the presentation-slot selection deadline. Dates and arrangements not yet listed remain TBD.
Assign yourself to a presentation slot using the Spring 2027 course scheduling spreadsheet when it is available. Its link will be added after setup.
Each student must observe and assess TWO other presentations (using the Project Assessment Form).
Your project grade is likely to suffer if:

you are not on time for your presentation or observations,
you are not prepared,
you do not observe at least two presentations, and/or
your observer feedback is not significant.

title: Project
text:
Important to keep in mind
Your presentation should be from the perspective that you are reporting to your colleagues why this article/method/result is or is not worth pursuing further.

Your audience is smart, but not specialized in your exact topic. Provide background, definitions, and motivation.
Be critical: clearly state strengths and weaknesses, and what assumptions matter.
You have access to tools (including AI) that were not commonly available a few years ago—so I will expect more polish and deeper checking.
I may not be an expert in what you present, but I expect you to be, and I will ask probing questions.
Your grade will depend on both:

how clearly you present, and
how well you answer questions.

title: Project
text:
Guidelines

Article review.

Choose a topic not already covered in lecture in essentially the same way.
Prefer papers with enough technical content to support real discussion (not just an application report).
Your job is to explain the idea, demonstrate it on a simple example, and assess it.

Simulation/data study.

Keep the scope appropriate: one sharp question is better than many shallow ones.
Predefine your evaluation metrics (e.g., coverage, power, MSE, false discovery rate).
Use clear plots/tables and report uncertainty when relevant.


General presentation advice:

Keep the big picture in view; don’t get bogged down in algebra.
Choose one simple example that illustrates the main point.
Look at your audience while speaking; do not read your notes.
Motivate your talk: background, prior work, and why anyone should care.
Discuss pros/cons and failure modes.
Don’t use too many slides; about one per minute is usually enough.
Don’t overload slides; prioritize figures/tables over dense text.
Include key formulas/figures directly in your slides rather than making the audience hunt in the paper.
Use your own words. Do not plagiarize.
Practice beforehand. Time yourself.

You will be assessed by your observers and by me using this form:
Project Assessment Form

title: MATH 574: Bayesian Computational Statistics
text:
Planned Topics
This is a provisional teaching outline, rather than a finalized syllabus. Textbooks, prerequisites, assessment policies, and optional topics remain to be confirmed.

Bayesian Inference: Likelihoods, priors, posteriors, and posterior prediction.
Monte Carlo Methods: Simulation, Monte Carlo integration, and assessment of sampling error.
Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis methods, computational diagnostics, and effective sample size.
Selected Topics: Possible Gaussian process models; scope to be decided.

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
text:
UNDER CONSTRUCTIONSpring 2027 preparation is in progress. Schedules, materials, and course policies are provisional.
This course uses a Git repository that includes submodules (shared libraries pulled in as separate Git repositories). To get everything working, you must clone the course repository and initialize the submodules.

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: Important: do not push to the course repository
text:
Important: do not push to the course repository
Students should assume the course repository is read-only:

Do not try to push changes to the course repository.
If you see errors like “permission denied” when pushing, that is expected.

You will not submit homework via Git. Git is used only to:

Obtain and update course materials
Experiment with class notebooks

When experimenting, consider working in copies of notebooks or in a separate directory so updates pull cleanly


If you want an online backup of your personal work, you may optionally use your own private repository or a fork (see below).

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
text:
Step 0: Prerequisites
You need:

Git installed
A way to authenticate with GitHub (either SSH or HTTPS)

Your instructor will provide the course repository URL. It looks like one of these:

SSH: git@github.com:ORG/MATHXXXSpring20YY.git
HTTPS: https://github.com/ORG/MATHXXXSpring20YY.git

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: Step 1: Clone the course repository with submodules
text:
Step 1: Clone the course repository with submodules
Choose one of the following.

Option A (recommended): clone with submodules in one step
Replace REPO_URL with the URL you were given.
git clone --recurse-submodules REPO_URL


Option B: clone first, then fetch submodules
git clone REPO_URL
cd MATHXXXSpring20YY
git submodule update --init --recursive

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: Step 2: Verify you have the submodule content
text:
Step 2: Verify you have the submodule content
From inside the course repository:
git submodule status
You should see one or more lines showing submodules and commit hashes. If you see errors or blank output, run:
git submodule update --init --recursive

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: Keeping your local copy updated during the semester
text:
Keeping your local copy updated during the semester
Do this whenever your instructor says “pull the latest changes.”
From inside the course repository:
git pull --ff-only
git submodule update --init --recursive
That second command is important: it updates submodules to the versions pinned by the course repository.

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: If you already made local changes
text:
If you already made local changes
If git pull --ff-only fails, it usually means you have local commits or uncommitted changes.
Check what changed:
git status

If you only changed files you don’t care about (quick reset)
git reset --hard
git pull --ff-only
git submodule update --init --recursive


If you want to keep your work
Commit your changes first so they are safely recorded locally.
git add -A
git commit -m "My work"
git pull --ff-only
git submodule update --init --recursive
If the pull still fails, you may need to resolve a merge conflict (ask for help).

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
section: Optional: fork workflow (push only to your own fork)
text:
Optional: fork workflow (push only to your own fork)
Use this only if you want to push your work to GitHub for backup/versioning.

One-time setup (fork + clone)

Fork the course repository on GitHub into your own GitHub account.
Clone your fork (not the instructor’s course repository) with submodules.

Replace FORK_URL with your fork’s URL:
git clone --recurse-submodules FORK_URL
cd MATHXXXSpring20YY

Add the instructor’s course repository as upstream so you can pull course updates.

Replace UPSTREAM_URL with the instructor’s course repository URL:
git remote add upstream UPSTREAM_URL
git remote -v


Getting updates from the instructor (sync upstream → your fork)
From inside your cloned fork:
git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge --ff-only upstream/main
git submodule update --init --recursive
git push
If the course repository uses a branch other than main (e.g., master), replace main above accordingly.

title: Git setup: clone the course repository and keep it updated
text:
Common issues and fixes

“fatal: not a git repository”
You’re not inside the course repository folder. Change into it:
cd MATHXXXSpring20YY


“Permission denied (publickey)” (SSH)
You’re using an SSH URL but your SSH key isn’t set up for GitHub. Use the HTTPS URL instead, or configure SSH.


Submodule errors after pulling
Re-run the submodule update:
git submodule update --init --recursive


You accidentally cloned without submodules
From inside the course repository:
git submodule update --init --recursive


Avoid updating submodules beyond what the instructor pinned
Students should not run git submodule update --remote unless explicitly instructed.

title: Big Statistics Questions We Ask
text:
UNDER CONSTRUCTIONSpring 2027 preparation is in progress. Schedules, materials, and course policies are provisional.





Filter by course

  
     MATH 476 Statistics
     MATH 563 Mathematical Statistics
     MATH 565 Monte Carlo Methods
  
  



Modeling

  Course(s)
  Big question



  476, 563, 565
  
    What is the population?
    All US adults? All future units from a production line? All students with bachelor's degree? All continuous functions on a given domain?
  



  476, 563, 565
  
    What features are we interested in?
    Mean? Variance? Quantiles? Regression function? Entire distribution?
  



  476, 563
  
    What does the model fail to capture?
    Explanatory variables? Interactions? Nonlinearities?
  



  476, 563
  
    Are the distributional assumptions correct?
    Normality? Skewness? Heavy tails? Independence?
  



Sampling

  Course(s)
  Big question



  476, 563, 565
  
    How do we sample from the population?
    Independent and identically distributed (IID)? Low discrepancy (LD)? Stratified sampling? Designed experiment?
  



  476, 563
  
    What can go wrong between intended and actual sampling?
    Nonresponse and missingness? Measurement error? Coverage error?
  



Point Estimation

  Course(s)
  Big question



  476, 563
  
    What is the estimand?
    
      Parameter vs functional of a distribution
      What does it mean in context?
      What is random, what is fixed?
    
  



  563
  
    What makes an estimator “optimal”?
    
      Loss functions and risk
      Invariance/equivariance (as appropriate)
      Benchmarks and lower bounds (when assumptions hold)
